payload.name: Attribute Relational Views to Speaking User
payload.description: During extraction in multi-party conversations, if one speaker explicitly states a view about someone or something, attribute the memory to that speaker, not to the conversation partner who agrees or responds.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly frames how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets feel like family'), record the speaker as the subject of the memory, regardless of whether another participant expresses agreement or a similar view.
If two participants each state their own view, create separate memories for each speaker with their own subject; do not merge one speaker's statement into the other's existing memory.
Before attributing a relational statement to an existing memory, verify that the memory's subject matches the speaker of the message; if not, create a new memory for the correct speaker.
Stop after capturing each speaker's explicit view once per relationship; do not duplicate or expand with agreement phrases.

solves: Extraction in multi-party conversations sometimes attributes one speaker's explicit relational view to the other participant, causing facts to be stored under the wrong person. This skill ensures statements are attributed to the actual speaker, preventing cross-speaker contamination of relationship memories.
